From: Anna Lee <anna@helios.ai>

Cc: Michael Turner <m.turner@helios.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for Helios Q4 — urgent allocation ask

Soojin,

Thanks again for the calibration call this morning. Quick summary from our side: Helios is prepared to commit to a 12-month dedicated pool starting Oct 1 that covers our peak inference needs for Q4 and into H1. We have a firm ARR figure tied to the commit (details attached to the procurement thread), but we urgently need clarity on how you will tranche GPU assignments across the quarter. In particular: 

- We need guaranteed minimum throughput for our streaming synth workloads during Nov–Dec holiday peaks.
- We are sensitive to preemption during scheduled hardware maintenance — any planned fallbacks?
- If another large customer requests burst capacity at the same time, how are decisions made?

Procurement asked we get an explicit tranche assignment and provisional SLOs in writing this week so they can start the internal approval. Can you propose an assignment (by tranche, with fallback) and confirm any operational exceptions?

Best,
Anna
Head of Platform Operations
Helios AI

Attachments: procurement_terms.pdf (referenced in their internal thread)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna@helios.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for Helios Q4 — urgent allocation ask

Anna — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. High-level response before I pull the ops team in: 

- We can commit to three tranches for Q4: Core (guaranteed 60% of committed vGPU throughput), Peak (additional 25% reserved but with a short-fallback policy), and Buffer (10% shared burst across customers).
- Fallbacks: scheduled maintenance windows will be published 30 days ahead; we will provide pre-warm capacity or migration to a compatible model variant during those windows.
- Contention policy: we use a weighted priority model tied to committed ARR and signed deal terms; in the case of simultaneous bursts, customers with higher tranche priority get preemptive allocation.

I'm looping Marcus (Dedicated Product) and Laura (CS) so we can formalize the tranche table and SLOs. Would you be able to confirm the exact peak throughput target (tokens/sec or p99 latency target) this week? That will let us size the GPU pool accurately.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead — Dedicated & Private
Redwood Inference

Soojin / Laura / Rishi — forwarding Anna's note and Soojin's reply. This is an operational escalation point: we have overlapping large commits in the same Oct–Dec window (Helios and a second prospect that just signaled a 24/7 model training inference BAU profile). We need to decide:

1) Whether to prioritize based on ARR / signed commitments vs. go-live date.
2) If we slice across customers (smaller guaranteed tranches, more buffer shared) or reserve contiguous GPU pools per customer.
3) How to codify the fallback (model-variant migration, cross-region warm standby, or soft-throttling).

Initial recommendation: reserve contiguous pools for customers with full-month committed capacity (Helios has the signed LOI), while allowing a smaller shared buffer for opportunistic burst. That minimizes cross-customer noisy-neighbor effects. But we need CS + infra input on migration feasibility and cost.

Marcus Lin
Director, Dedicated Products
Redwood Inference

Team — attached is our proposed tranche assignment and operational playbook (Tranche_Assignments_v2.xlsx) plus a one-pager summary (Helios_Q4_commitment_summary.pdf). Highlights: 

- Core tranche: 60% guaranteed throughput (isolated vGPU pool), 99.9% monthly availability SLO (excludes scheduled maintenance).
- Peak tranche: 25% reserved; in sustained multi-customer burst events, Peak will be queued behind Core based on ARR-weighted priority.
- Buffer tranche: 15% shared burst pool with soft-throttling after 15 continuous minutes at >95% utilization.
- Fallback options: cross-region warm standby (where region capacity available), model-variant migration (documented rollback path), or temporary traffic shaping with credit compensation for SLA misses.
- Maintenance policy: we will publish planned maintenance 30 days in advance and offer a 4-hour pre-warm/ migration window for impacted customers.

Action items: 
- Anna / Helios: confirm acceptance of the tranche percentages and p99 target by Aug 20 so legal can finalize the addendum.
- Redwood Ops (Rishi): run a sizing check against Helios's sample traces and confirm required vGPU count by Aug 18.
- CS (Laura): schedule a joint runbook walkthrough with Helios the week of Sep 6.

Attachments referenced: Tranche_Assignments_v2.xlsx (sheets: summary, tranche-mapping, fallback-playbook), Helios_Q4_commitment_summary.pdf

Thanks — I will track the signature and post the finalized tranche mapping to the HubSpot deal page.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
